newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-BECKER HOPES TO PLAY FOR UP TO THREE MORE YEARS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER HOPES TO PLAY FOR UP TO THREE MORE YEARS.

text.p: Former Wimbledon champion Boris Becker on Saturday reassured fans he was not about to drop out of tennis and said he hoped to play for another two or three years.
"If my body holds out, I would love to play for another two or three years," Becker told the mass-circulation Bild daily.
"Why should I stop," said the 29-year-old German, who has been plagued by injury in the last few years. "By the age of 18 I had already won Wimbledon twice. I could have stopped then."
"I want to be on top form again in a month... Then I will be a title contender. Wimbledon is still on my mind," he said.
The world number 12 said even if he won Wimbledon this year, that would not mean the end of his career. "Tennis is just like normal life. Sometimes you're on top, sometimes at the bottom."
After a two-month break because of a tendinitis, Becker crashed out of the Monte Carlo Open last month.
Fellow German and ex-Wimbledon champion Michael Stich, 28, shocked fans on Friday by announcing he would retire from tennis later this year because of a recurring shoulder injury.
